title: us watchdog conduct review whistleblower warning mail in voting rules 2026 09 08
text:
WASHINGTON, Sept 8 (Reuters) - The U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General said on Tuesday it plans ​to conduct an independent review of allegations from a whistleblower ‌who has warned proposed USPS mail-in voting restrictions could result in thousands of legal ballots being discarded.
On Friday, a federal judge in Boston extended a ban ​stopping President Donald Trump's administration from implementing a new USPS ​rule that would tighten mail-in voting requirements ahead of the ⁠November congressional elections.
Last week, President Donald Trump's administration asked the Supreme Court ​to let it enforce the new USPS rule on use of mail-in ​ballots.
Lawmakers have urged USPS to halt work on new mail-in voting rules, saying they threaten the integrity of the November congressional elections. They cited a whistleblower who ​warned that USPS' planned “verification” systems "risk collapsing the absentee ballot system and ​disenfranchising millions of Americans."
The USPS regulation would impose new voter-specific data and ballot ‌envelope ⁠standards, and potentially refuse the delivery of ballots that do not comply, which critics say could disrupt thousands of legitimate votes as the November 3 vote approaches.
Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain control ​of Congress in ​the elections. Critics ⁠say restricting mail-in ballots would disproportionately benefit Republicans given that Democratic voters traditionally have been more likely ​to use mail-in ballots.
Under the new USPS rule, states must ​provide ⁠lists

 of mail ballot recipients to the postal service and use agency-approved outbound and return ballot mail envelopes outfitted with unique barcodes. The postal ⁠service ​could then refuse to send out ballots ​that do not comply with the new standards or are associated with voters who do ​not appear on the lists.
